title: Ignite 2026: Windows Hello event logs and passwordless updates
summary: Microsoft listed Windows sign-in changes aimed at passwordless rollouts, most of them in the Windows 11 Insider Experimental channel: PIN offered alongside Face or Fingerprint (PIN first after a restart), new Windows Hello event logs (HelloForBusiness/Operational and the Security log) that show whether a device was unlocked with Face, Fingerprint or PIN, and IAKerb. Update 20 November: web sign-in for Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices, the automatic screen-brightness option for face sign-in and the NFC tap location indicator shipped in the KB5132057 non-security preview (19 November, gradual rollout), so they are no longer Insider-only. Coming to Insiders this month: passkey security key management, a Security page in Settings, remote lock, BitLocker TPM + PIN for standard users (Intune-managed) and the Pluton key storage provider.
why: The event logs give you evidence of how users actually sign in, which helps audits and help desk troubleshooting. 'PIN first after restart' changes what users see every morning, so it needs communication before it reaches production. Web sign-in for hybrid joined devices removes a blocker for shared and frontline devices.
todo: Do now: if you run Insider devices, collect the new Windows Hello event logs in a pilot and decide which events to forward to your SIEM.
Prepare user communication for the PIN-first behaviour after restart.
Wait: most items are Insider Experimental channel or 'coming soon'. Announced, not verified on retail builds; watch the Windows release health page and Message Center.
effective_note: Insider Experimental channel for most items; web sign-in for hybrid join, face brightness and NFC indicator shipped in KB5132057 (19 Nov, gradual rollout).
